solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Singer collapsed in pain, upset by something eaten

indicators.note: the shuffled singer letters are placed inside the word for pain
upset means overturned, so the word for pain is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a pang is a sharp pain

indicators.note: something collapsed has lost its shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A singer keels over in agony after something they ate disagreed with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something eaten' is a ginger biscuit; 'upset' looks like 'unwell' after the meal, but it turns the pain word backwards, and 'collapsed' reworks the singer's letters to go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger biscuit with a snap to it is a sweet treat that people eat.

clue.text: Locals having pronouncedly influential connections

indicators.note: pronouncedly means as spoken, so the phrase is what is heard, not written

parts.note: people with an in, or ins, have influential connections

explanation.surface: The pubs nearby have friends in high places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locals' is the British word for neighbourhood pubs, which is what inns are.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a Briton's nearest pub, and old pubs are often called inns.

clue.text: With guard dog, were almost all returning. Stopped being silly

parts.note: G is a standard abbreviation for guard, as in team positions

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the shortened words are read backwards
almost all means each word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a guard dog finds everyone heading back and finally acts sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' trims the last letter from each of the two words; 'returning' then reads the pair backwards, after the G for guard.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature is to stop acting childishly, an idiom for leaving foolishness behind.

clue.text: Understanding there will be a buffet, with drink

parts.note: to buffet is to strike, and a rap is a blow
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: There'll be a buffet meal with something to drink, it is understood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a spread of food, but it is a verb meaning hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close mutual sympathy, the understanding between people who get on.

clue.text: Catch and it may scratch you

definitions.meaning: to catch a criminal is to nab or collar them

explanation.surface: A warning that catching something may get you scratched.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for arresting a culprit, and also the hard plate at a fingertip that can scratch.

clue.text: Thinks better, in addendum, to direct elsewhere

indicators.note: the word for redirecting sits within the addendum abbreviation

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an addendum to a letter
to refer someone is to send them on to another

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders, adding a postscript that sends the reader elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer one option is to think it better than the alternatives, a synonym.

clue.text: Miss for only a short time

definitions.text: Miss for only a short time

parts.words: Miss for only a short time
parts.note: a girl wed very young keeps the title Miss only briefly before becoming Mrs

explanation.surface: Seems to be about missing someone briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like the verb of longing, but it is the title of an unmarried girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A very young wife held the unmarried title only briefly before her wedding.

clue.text: He hopes to be well-compensated for his investigations

definitions.text: He hopes to be well-compensated for his investigations

parts.words: He hopes to be well-compensated for his investigations
parts.note: a searcher for gold or oil hopes a well or mine will pay off his digging

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a private detective hoping for a good fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-compensated' hides a pun: an oil well that rewards the searcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A miner exploring for gold or oil hopes his digging strikes it rich.

clue.text: Drink one may be angling for

explanation.surface: A drink someone may be hinting they would like.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for tea, and also a freshwater fish related to trout.

clue.text: With log lever up, showing initiative

parts.note: to log data is to enter it
to prise is to lever something open or up

explanation.surface: Someone shows initiative by heaving a log up with a lever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log' looks like a piece of wood, but it is the verb to record.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise is readiness to start new projects, the same quality as initiative.

clue.text: Deals with blank square, putting in first letter of 'ruffles'

indicators.note: putting in means the letter is inserted into the word for filling squares

parts.note: a solver fills a blank square in a grid

indicators.note: first letter of picks only the opening letter of the quoted word

explanation.surface: A crossword solver fills an empty square with the letter R.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted word does double duty, giving its first letter and also defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffles are gathered decorative edgings on clothing, which are frills.

clue.text: Do they undermine the strength of the Army?

definitions.text: Do they undermine the strength of the Army?

parts.words: Do they undermine the strength of the Army?
parts.note: military engineers literally dig mines and trenches under enemy positions

explanation.surface: Asks whether some group is weakening the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undermine' looks figurative, but these soldiers literally dig under things; they are part of the army's strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Military engineers who dig tunnels and mines are given this name in the British Army.

clue.text: Providing a cast-iron case is the stock in trade

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit that cannot fail is a powerful suit
one's usual speciality, the thing one does best

explanation.surface: Supplying watertight arguments is someone's business speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit read literally as powerful, and the idiom for a personal speciality or forte.

clue.text: Tidy up while you ring restaurant for take-out?

definitions.meaning: phoning a restaurant, you place an order for food

explanation.surface: Clean the place while you phone for a takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging things neatly, and literally lodging a food request by phone.

clue.text: Things worth seeing, you say … lots

indicators.note: you say means the phrase is taken as it is heard spoken

parts.note: sights are things worth seeing

explanation.surface: Seems to be someone claiming there are lots of attractions.
explanation.definitionFit: Building lots are plots of land, and such plots are building sites.

clue.text: Plant shown by book to grow in random fashion

parts.note: a rambling plant spreads untidily

explanation.surface: A gardening book shows a plant that grows all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackberry bush, a thorny plant, is a classic example of this.

clue.text: In short, rush off. Brush fire spreading

indicators.note: off means the letters of the word rush are taken away
a fire spreading is moving about, so the remaining letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A quick warning: get away fast, the scrub fire is spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush off' takes R, U, S, H from BRUSHFIRE, leaving BFIRE, and 'spreading' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To put it briefly is to say it in short, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: They draw from banks

definitions.meaning: people who tie a match draw it, so they are those who tie
banks of seats are rows rising one above another

explanation.surface: Seems to be about people withdrawing money from banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as those who tie a game, and also rising rows like banks of seats.

clue.text: 'It's traditional procedure, OK?' you say

indicators.note: you say tells us the word is the one heard spoken

parts.note: right is agreement, like OK

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a custom is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony carried out by custom, such as a religious ritual.

clue.text: With 'Good', off we went to get a drink

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good in crosswords

indicators.note: off means the letters of we are taken away from the following word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a friend called Good set off for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes WE from WENT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a measure of beer, the usual pub serving.

clue.text: Put off returning again, no longer hungry

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: refed means fed again

explanation.surface: Someone delays coming back now their appetite is satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone something is to put it off until later.

clue.text: Misery of French with their capital destroyed

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: a city destroyed is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Paris is the French capital

explanation.surface: The French are in misery because their capital has been ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a deep wretchedness.

clue.text: In foreign city, can drift into an affaire

indicators.note: In means the shuffled letters go inside the city

parts.note: Rome is a foreign city to a British solver

indicators.note: to drift is to wander about, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: In some foreign city, a visitor may drift into a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: An affaire, borrowed from French, is a love affair, which is a romance.

clue.text: They take issue over our being too busy to cope

definitions.text: They take issue over our being too busy to cope

parts.words: They take issue over our being too busy to cope
parts.note: issue means children, whom childminders take over when parents are too busy

explanation.surface: Seems to be about people complaining that we are overstretched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take issue' looks like disagreeing, but issue means offspring, which these carers take over.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's carers employed by families look after the offspring when parents are busy.

clue.text: Don't, because pursued by wild animal

indicators.note: pursued by means the first word is followed by the animal

parts.note: for can mean because
a bear is a wild animal

explanation.surface: A warning not to do something, since a wild beast is giving chase.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to refrain from acting, so as an instruction it means do not.

clue.text: To get cured, he's taking a chance

definitions.meaning: a gambler who bets takes a chance

explanation.surface: A man gambles in the hope of getting well.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovered from illness, and also someone who wagers money on an outcome.

clue.text: Runt tagging on to mum: terribly prim

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: terribly means badly done, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A small child trails after a very prim mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother, but it means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimp is a small weedy person, as is a runt.

clue.text: Be careful. It's booby-trapped, according to reports

indicators.note: according to reports means as heard said

parts.note: a mined area is booby-trapped with explosives

explanation.surface: A warning to tread carefully because the area is booby-trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind the step is an instruction to be careful, so mind means take care.

clue.text: Does it warn to keep away from the bull?

definitions.text: Does it warn to keep away from the bull?

parts.words: Does it warn to keep away from the bull?
parts.note: a car's hooter warns people off, and a bull has a pointed one on its head

explanation.surface: Asks whether a warning sign tells walkers to avoid a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooter that warns people, and also the pointed growth a bull might gore you with.

clue.text: Giving a fabrication to people when there's an estrangement

parts.note: a lie is a fabrication
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Someone lies to a whole people, causing a rift.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is the state of being cut off from others, a synonym of estrangement.

clue.text: Object I bumped into, turning

indicators.note: turning means going round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to bump into someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: Someone describes colliding with a thing while turning a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single thing or article, which an object also is.

clue.text: Steer you should ignore from herd scattering, wayward

indicators.note: a herd scattering breaks up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: erring means going astray, wayward

explanation.surface: A cowboy should ignore one bullock straying from the scattering herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a young bull, but it means a pointer or tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A false clue that leads you astray is a misleading tip, a steer to disregard.
